newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India cancels and reissues Cochin naphtha tender.
newsitem.headline: India cancels and reissues Cochin naphtha tender.

text.p: Low bids have prompted state-owned Indian Oil Corp State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) to cancel its tender to sell 20,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) lifting April 30-May 2 from Cochin on the west coast due to low offers, industry sources said on Monday.
The tender closed on April 17 and bids were valid for one day.

An industry source said IOC has reoffered the product in a fresh tender, but increased the volume to 30,000 tonnes and moved the loading dates to May 6-7 in the hope that price improve. The tender closes April 24 and is valid for a day.
Demand for HAN, which is used in the production of gasoline, was poor and lead to low offers, traders said.

In its last tender for HAN, lifting from Madras on the east coast between April 25-27, IOC only managed to secure a $31 discount to Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, compared to a $22.28 discount it received for a March 27-29 lifting cargo.
IOC's last HAN tender from Cochin, lifting April 1-3, was awarded at $19.08 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
